issues.quote: `localhost` is a name that always means the machine you are on, usually address `127.0.0.1`.
issues.text: New in this pass. "usually" makes me pause: if not 127.0.0.1, what else, and is it still my machine? Nothing later says. I can go on, because every later step uses the name localhost or the 127.0.0.1 hosts line, never another number, so the main idea is not affected.
issues.fix: Add a few words after "usually address `127.0.0.1`" saying that whichever address it has, it still means this machine.

issues.quote: Only the HTTPS port runs encryption, hence `donhang.local:8443` instead of `localhost:8080`.
issues.text: Carried from round 3 (section unchanged). Section 2 showed my browser failing on donhang.local, yet the script uses that name with no comment; I learn why it works inside the lab only at the end of section 6.
issues.fix: Add half a sentence to the step 3 bullet: "the lab lists `donhang.local` in its own hosts file, so the name works for the script".

issues.quote: Step 4: `-D -` prints what came back instead of the page, and `-o /dev/null` throws the page away.
issues.text: Carried from round 3 (section unchanged). "what came back instead of the page" confuses me: the page also came back. I only work out that it means the lines sent before the page from the "..." note under the output.
issues.fix: Write "`-D -` prints the lines the server sends before the page" and keep the rest of the sentence.

issues.quote: B->>S: ask again for each file the page embeds
issues.text: Carried from round 3 (section unchanged). Every earlier ask has a return arrow, but the last has none, and the "draw" step named in the chain definition is not in the diagram.
issues.fix: Say in the paragraph after the diagram that each embedded file comes back in its own response, as the earlier arrows show, and that drawing is not shown.

issues.quote: You start the lab — the programs `scripts/up.sh` runs on your machine, with names and addresses of its own, so it behaves like a separate machine — and open `http://localhost:8080/index.html` in your browser;
issues.text: Carried from round 3. The opening sentence holds two inserted definitions (lab, localhost) around the main action, and now a "usually" too; I read it twice to find what I actually do. "the machine, the connection, or Caddy" leaves me unsure which machine: mine or the lab.
issues.fix: Split into two sentences: first what the lab is, then "Open `http://localhost:8080/index.html` …"; write "your machine" in the colleague sentence if that is meant.
